Hi Liam / Sofia,

Thanks again for the time earlier — good conversation and appreciate the clarity on the internal goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the POC moving: 

Proposed success criteria (draft):
- Reduce average inference latency for batch QA checks from ~450ms to <=200ms
- Achieve >=92% retrieval+generation accuracy on the 500-sample evaluation set you shared
- Demonstrate stable throughput at your target concurrency (50 concurrent requests) for 1 hour

Evaluation plan highlights (attached):
- Week 0 (prep): data access + config, baseline runs
- Week 1–3 (trial): iterative tuning, weekly readouts
- Week 4 (final): consolidated results and handoff

Suggested timeline / milestone schedule:
- Kickoff: week of June 22 (propose Tue Jun 23, 10:00–11:00 PT)
- Weekly check-ins: Wed 30-min sync (status, blockers, next actions)
- Final readout: Jul 20 — 45-min presentation + decision meeting

Ownership (Redwood / Acme):
- Redwood AE / PM: Marissa Cole (coordination, commercial)
- Redwood SE: Nikhil Sharma (technical leads, runbooks)
- Acme PM: Liam O'Neill (success criteria, evaluation sign-off)
- Acme Data Owner: Sofia Ramirez (data access/PII questions)

Attachments: POC success criteria (draft) and Acme evaluation plan spreadsheet.

Could you please: 
1) Confirm the success criteria above (or suggest edits)
2) Confirm availability for the kickoff on Tue Jun 23 at 10:00 PT or suggest 2 alternative slots
3) Grant read-only access to the sample dataset (S3 path or secure share) for the SE team before kickoff

I’ll coordinate calendar invites and send an updated evaluation plan after we lock the date.

Thanks,

Thanks — quick technical notes before kickoff: 

Pre-kickoff checklist (SE):
- Read-only S3 credentials or secure share of the 500-sample evaluation set (please include a small README)
- Network egress allowances for Redwood test agents (we'll provide IP ranges)
- Example prompt templates and current baseline logs (if available)
- Expected QPS profile (50 concurrent, bursts to 80) and auth method for API calls

On the trial runs themselves I plan to:
- Run baseline using your sample set, record latency/throughput and error rates
- Enable lightweight caching and measure impact (we'll show token-level cost delta)
- Iterate quantization/profile suggestions if we hit memory constraints

If you can share the S3 path and add nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai as a principal for read-only access that will unblock the SE workstreams. Happy to sync 30 minutes before the kickoff if the team wants a quick technical pre-check.
